# AgentObs

> A local-first observability and control layer for AI coding agents. Unlike
> every other tool in this space, AgentObs can refuse a tool call: it enforces
> spend limits, token limits and command policy *before* the call runs, rather
> than reporting cost after it is already spent.

Install: `npm install -g @klars/agentobs` then `agentobs init`.
Requires Node.js 22.5 or newer. Open source (MIT), no account, no telemetry.
Source: https://github.com/klars-ai/agentobs

## What problem it solves

Agent tooling is almost entirely read-only. Tools like ccusage and
Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor parse the same local transcripts and tell you what
you already spent. None of them can stop anything, because reporting on usage
does not require knowing your limit. AgentObs asks for the limit, which is
what makes both enforcement and forecasting possible.

## Core capabilities

- **Budgets that block.** `agentobs budget set --daily 5 --block` refuses tool
  calls once the limit is hit. Periods: daily, weekly, monthly, and the
  rolling 5-hour block that matches Anthropic's own rate-limit window.
  Denominated in USD or in tokens, so Max and Pro subscribers - who have no
  dollar cost - can still cap usage.
- **Forecasting.** `agentobs forecast` projects time-to-limit from the burn
  rate of recent real activity, e.g. "at $4.14/hour you hit the limit in
  44 min". Burn rate is measured over active minutes, not wall-clock, because
  averaging idle time understates a live session several-fold.
- **Command policy.** Glob rules over tool inputs deny destructive commands and
  secret-file reads before execution, e.g. `rm -rf /` or reading `.env`.
- **Interactive approvals.** A `needs_approval` rule holds a call and notifies
  you. Approval is fingerprinted over the tool name plus its exact input, so
  approving `rm -rf ./build` never authorises `rm -rf /`. Approvals expire
  after 60 minutes. This is approve-then-retry, not a live prompt: the first
  attempt is always refused, because a hook has no channel to the user.
- **Secret redaction.** Vendor-specific patterns (AWS, Anthropic, OpenAI,
  GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Stripe, Resend, Google, npm, JWT, PEM) plus
  structural rules for assignments, CLI flags, auth headers and URL
  credentials. Nothing unredacted is ever written to disk.
- **MCP server.** `claude mcp add agentobs -- agentobs mcp` lets the agent
  query its own usage - you can ask Claude "am I close to my limit?" and it
  answers from real local data.
- **Statusline.** A compact status-bar line showing the real 5-hour rate limit
  from Anthropic's own payload, the tightest budget, a countdown, and context
  usage.
- **Multi-agent import.** Reads Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenAI Codex
  CLI, Gemini CLI and OpenCode logs. Sources are declarative, so an unknown
  agent can be added with a JSON definition and no code.
- **Dashboard.** A local web dashboard with light and dark themes.

## Honesty commitments

These are design rules, not marketing:

- Only Claude Code's log format is marked `verified`; the others were written
  from documentation and are labelled `unverified`, because claiming support
  that silently records nothing is the worst failure an observability tool can
  have.
- An unpriced model renders as `-`, never `$0.00`. Unknown is not zero.
- Cache reads are billed at 0.1x and counted separately from fresh input,
  because summing them inflates totals by orders of magnitude.

## Privacy

Everything is local: a SQLite database under `~/.agentobs`. No account, no
API key, no telemetry, no network calls. Secrets are redacted before storage.
